4.0.s.en: (1) The rest is not accomplished on the Sabbath

4.0.0.en: A promise left us of entering into his rest: God's promise to believers of eternal rest.

4.0.1.en: Come short of it: that is, not obtain it.

4.0.2.en: God promised His people in ancient times that they would enter the Promised Land, and not all the people obtained this promise, because most of those who murmured and refused to enter fell and died in the wilderness of Sinai. So the Apostle warns us of the necessity of caution lest we fail to obtain God's promise of rest like those who did not enter.

4.0.3.en: The fear of God gives you carefulness and distance from sin, so you receive God's mercies and support, and it urges you on to spiritual striving, so that by the grace of God you secure a place in the Kingdom. Remember God, who sees you, when the thought of sin fights you, so that you quickly move away from it.

4.1.0.en: The word preached: God's promise and good news to His people in ancient times of entering the Promised Land.

4.1.1.en: St. Paul warns us that we have heard the good news of Christ the Savior as the Jews heard in ancient times the good news of entering the Promised Land, but most of them did not enter because of their unbelief and their murmuring against Moses, so they died in the wilderness (Num 14:1-3).

4.2.0.en: The works were finished from the foundation of the world: God's creation of the world, including the Promised Land, and likewise the Kingdom of Heaven.

4.2.1.en: We who believe enter into eternal rest because of our faith in Christ, but the people of Israel in ancient times did not enter the Promised Land because of their unbelief, although God had finished the creation of everything before He created man.

4.3.0.en: The first announcement of rest in the Holy Bible was on the seventh day (Gen 2:2), when God finished the creation of the world. The rest here does not mean ceasing from work, but God's joy in what He had made, because Christ says, “My Father worketh hitherto, and I work” (Jn 5:17).

4.4.0.en: In this place: that is, on the Sabbath day, which was a type of the eternal rest.

4.4.1.en: The Jews did not enjoy rest on the Sabbath day because they:

4.4.2.en: 1- Understood rest to mean ceasing from work and not doing good.

4.4.3.en: 2- Did not believe in Christ the Savior, who is the Lord of the Sabbath and the Giver of true rest.

4.4.4.en: Faith in Christ gives you reassurance in all your steps, and makes you feel the sweetness of fellowship with Him and leads you to the constant enjoyment of eternity.

4.5.s.en: (2) The rest is not completed in the Promised Land

4.5.0.en: Seeing therefore it remaineth: there is something other than the rest of the Sabbath and the land of Canaan, and it is the Kingdom of Heaven. Some must enter therein: those who believe in Christ.

4.5.1.en: They to whom it was first preached: the Jews whom Moses called to enter the Promised Land and who refused because of their unbelief in the power of God that overcomes the enemies before them.

4.5.2.en: Entered not in because of unbelief: they did not enter the Promised Land because of their disobedience to God by the hand of Moses.

4.5.3.en: It is understood from the foregoing that those who believe in Christ will enter the heavenly Kingdom, whereas the children of Israel, whom God called to enter the Promised Land as a type of entering the Kingdom of Heaven, murmured and did not obey God, so they did not enter.

4.6.0.en: Again, he limiteth a certain day: a day in which the rest of the Kingdom is promised.

4.6.1.en: Saying in David: that is, in the Book of Psalms, most of which David wrote (Ps 95:7, 8). To day, after so long a time: the day is the days of David, which is after a period of about 500 years from the children of Israel's entering the Promised Land. David is of course speaking of another rest than the Promised Land which they had entered before.

4.6.2.en: As it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts: David calls to all mankind that if they hear the good news of Christ the Savior, they should not harden their hearts and reject it, lest they be deprived of entering the Kingdom of Heaven.

4.6.3.en: Because the true rest is in the Kingdom of Heaven, David, who lived a long time after the entering of the Promised Land, calls to mankind to believe in Christ the Savior, who gives them eternal life.

4.7.0.en: Paul affirms that if the true rest were in the land of Canaan by the hand of Joshua, David would not have spoken about another rest which we enter by faith in Christ if we hear the good news of Him.

4.8.0.en: It is understood from the foregoing that there is another rest for the people of God, that is, the Jews, which is neither the Sabbath nor the land of Canaan, and it is the eternal rest which the new people of God receive, that is, those who believe in Christ the Savior.

4.9.0.en: For he that is entered into his rest: the believer in Christ who has entered into eternity.

4.9.1.en: Hath ceased from his own works: the works of spiritual striving and the labors of this life.

4.9.2.en: As God did from his: as God rested on the seventh day after completing the creation of the world and rejoiced in what He had completed, so also the believers when they enter heaven rejoice in being with God after their striving on earth.

4.9.3.en: The believer in Christ who enters the blessed eternity enjoys true rest, like the rest which God feels after completing the creation of the world, which is spiritual rest.

4.9.4.en: Do not be much preoccupied with the comfort and pampering of your body, for all this is temporary and passing. As much as you are able, give yourself the opportunity to pray and serve even at the partial expense of the body's comfort, and you will enjoy fellowship with God.

4.10.0.en: Since we have been assured that true rest is in Christ the Savior, who gives it to us in the heavens, let us strive spiritually to leave every sin and hold fast to faith and a life of righteousness so that we have a place in heaven, and not fall into disobedience to God's commandments as the Jews disobeyed in ancient times, but take warning from their unbelief.

4.11.0.en: What helps us in striving is that the words of God in the Holy Bible are:

4.11.1.en: Quick, and powerful: they do not grow old but are always strong and affect souls.

4.11.2.en: Sharper than any twoedged sword: very sharp, more than the two-edged sword that cuts to the right and to the left, for it exposes all faults.

4.11.3.en: Piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart: deep in its effect, reaching the depths of man's soul and spirit as the sharp sword reaches the depths of the body, so it exposes the sins of thought and heart and calls man to repentance.

4.11.4.en: The word of God is the best support for the spiritual striver in uncovering his sins, so he moves away from them and returns to God to grow in every good work.

4.12.0.en: St. Paul affirms that God, the Creator of all creatures, knows all that is within them because He is their Creator and Governor, and this calls us in turn to the fear of God and the rejection of sin.

4.13.0.en: A great high priest: Aaron the high priest was the one who entered alone into the Holy Place, but Christ, the great priest of the New Testament, is the One who enters alone into the heavens to prepare a place for us.

4.13.1.en: That is passed into the heavens: the high priest in ancient times entered with blood and passed into the Holy of Holies to make atonement for the people, and this was a type of Christ. And when he says the heavens, he means that He passed through all the heavens that mankind knows, whether the heaven of the birds or the planets or the highest heavens, to reach the heaven of heavens, that is, the Kingdom.

4.13.3.en: In our striving to reach heaven, let us hold fast to the word of God and His fear and also to faith in Christ, our High Priest and Savior, who has prepared a place for us in heaven and helps us until He brings us to it.

4.14.0.en: The One who encourages us to hold fast the faith, that is, our Christ, is not a God far from us, but became incarnate and endured sufferings like us to make us feel His nearness to us and His compassion for our weakness, and at the same time He is without sin, that is, able to save us from it.

4.15.0.en: The Apostle Paul urges us to boldness and confidence in approaching our great God, not only God seated on His throne, but the One who pours out His grace on us because He loved us and died for us to forgive us our sins and support us with His mercy at all times and give us His help in every affliction in which we take refuge in Him.

4.15.1.en: Trust in the love of God your Redeemer and draw near to Him however great your sins and however much afflictions increase, for He is able to rescue you because He loves you and will not leave you, so He lifts you out of your troubles and supports you on the path of your life until He brings you to Him .. trust in your victory through Him over all difficulties.

4.15.2.en: Comparison between the Levitical priesthood and the priesthood of Christ

5.0.0.en: The Apostle Paul speaks about the characteristics of the Levitical priesthood, that is, Aaron and all the high priests his successors, who are taken from weak men for the service of God, and offer sacrifices on behalf of the people to obtain forgiveness of their sins from God.

5.1.0.en: For every high priest: these are from among men and subject to human weakness, so they are able to feel and have compassion on sinners who are foolish and far away, deviating from the Law of God.

5.2.0.en: Because the Jewish high priest is a weak man liable to sin, he offers sacrifices also for his own sins and not only for the sins of the people. This is of course unlike Christ, who does not need a sacrifice for Himself because He is righteous and holy.

5.3.0.en: This office of high priesthood no one can take or appoint himself to, but he must have a call from God, like Aaron, who was called by name by God to this office: “Take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office” (Ex 28:1).

5.3.1.en: Christ felt our weaknesses and bore them though He is the Strong. Is it not fitting for us, being men subject to weakness like them, to feel the weaknesses of people?!

5.4.0.en: Likewise, the Lord Christ did not take the office of high priest from Himself, but God the Father called Him to this implicitly when the Divine inspiration revealed to us in (Ps 2:7) the depth of the relationship between God the Father and Christ the Son, which must be present in a high priest, the ability to bind his people to God.

5.4.1.en: And in the fullness of time the Father sent Him to become incarnate and redeem mankind by saying, “this day have I begotten thee”; this is a functional division within the divine Self, that the hypostasis of the Son should become incarnate to accomplish redemption. If the Jews consider Aaron a high priest because God called him, then all the more Christ is the true High Priest, whom Aaron symbolizes, because God called Him to this service as the psalm declares.

5.5.0.en: Likewise also the calling of the Lord Christ to the priesthood, that is, His worthiness and ability to accomplish the priestly work as God incarnate, appears in (Ps 110:4), when the Father addresses the incarnate Son, “Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec” (who is a priest in the Old Testament, to be explained in detail in chapter seven), and nothing was said about his lineage or his death, so as to be a type of the eternal, everlasting priesthood of the Lord.

5.6.0.en: This distinction of the priesthood of Christ appeared with power in the days of His being in the flesh on earth, when the Lord Christ offered, as priest and intercessor and representative of mankind, prayers and supplications with tears and intense groaning on behalf of His people, who are the whole world, knowing and feeling the weakness of mankind; so that God would accept the deliverance of the world from death in the person of the Lord Christ as priest and representative of mankind, and it appeared and was confirmed to us that He is the true High Priest who can deliver us from death in His person and by His atoning intercession for us before God, since God answered Him, because He is without sin to veil His voice and will from God, for He and God are one. His crying out in the garden of Gethsemane shows how severe were the sufferings He endured as a High Priest offering Himself as a sacrifice for the redemption of His people, and because He is righteous and without sin, the Father heard Him, that is, He was able to take away the sins of mankind and redeemed them by His death and then rose from the dead, that is, the Father raised Him, answering His cry; for the divinity raised the humanity because it is united with it even while it was in the tomb.

5.6.1.en: This verse shows the true humanity of Christ in His enduring sufferings and at the same time shows His divinity in His perfect righteousness and His resurrection from the dead.

5.7.0.en: Learned obedience: that is, He showed obedience.

5.7.1.en: Although the Lord Christ is the Son of God and one with Him in essence, out of His love for us and His knowledge and feeling of our need, He set aside His glory and showed His submission to the will of the just God in enduring all the sufferings on behalf of mankind to the death of the Cross.

5.8.0.en: After Christ completed redemption and then rose and ascended into heaven, everyone who believes in Him and obeys His commandments and submits to Him and receives Him by faith enjoys the eternal salvation which He Himself accomplished for us.

5.9.0.en: By the entering of the believers into eternity the completion of Christ's work as High Priest appears, to which God the Father called Him, and He remains a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec by the glorification of His children in heaven as their Savior and Redeemer. The priesthood of Aaron was temporary, by offering sacrifices that symbolize Christ, but the priesthood of Christ is eternal after the rite and order of Melchisedec, whose explanation will come in chapter seven.

5.10.0.en: This Melchisedec, who is a type of Christ, O Hebrews, we have much explanation concerning him, but we will not be able to speak of it now because you will not understand what will be said about him, since as a result of the hesitation and doubt that afflicted you in the faith and the desire of some of you to return to Jewish worship, your ears have become unable to understand the deeper matters.

5.11.0.en: For the time: your knowledge about Christ from the prophecies and types of the Old Testament.

5.11.1.en: The first principles of the oracles of God: the fundamentals of faith in Christ.

5.11.2.en: Milk: the simple, easy food that is given to infants, that is, the elementary teachings of faith in Christ. Strong meat: the deep teaching about Christ.

5.11.3.en: Paul rebukes the Christians of Jewish origin for their failure to grasp the deep teaching about Christ because of their holding to the types of the Old Testament such as circumcision and their doubts about Christ. For instead of eating the strong food, that is, the deep teaching about Christ, and teaching others who are beginners, they themselves became beginners in the faith and need to have the fundamentals of the Christian faith established, and that the priesthood of Christ is what all the types of the Old Testament symbolized.

5.12.0.en: He continues his rebuke of them in that their continuing to accept only the fundamentals of the faith hinders them from going deeper into the life of Christian righteousness and spiritual growth.

5.13.0.en: Of full age: those who are steadfast in the faith and care about spiritual growth.

5.13.2.en: Senses: he means the inner senses, that is, spiritual understanding.

5.13.3.en: The Apostle Paul clarifies that the deep teaching about the Christian life is given to those who are steadfast in the faith and care about the salvation of their souls, in rejecting evil such as pride and doubt, for through their training in spiritual striving they easily accept what develops their relationship with God and increase in doing good, unlike the beginners who are still discussing the fundamentals of faith.

5.13.4.en: O High Priest of heaven, Jesus Christ, Son of God, who accepted all the sufferings for my sake, who stand in the Holy of Holies of heaven, have mercy on me, sick with sin, to grant me a share with You in Your Kingdom. You who bore my weakness in Yourself to turn it into strength, and took my sin to clothe me with the garment of Your righteousness, O High Priest of good things to come, I praise You because You had compassion on me. I thank You, O compassionate High Priest, who are able to have pity on my weakness; teach me to obey as You obeyed, teach me to share in Your sufferings, that this may be for me eternal salvation. Amen.

5.13.5.en: Beware of apostasy and hold fast to good works and hope
